docs: move the wiki into docs/ and bring it up to date

The wiki had drifted badly since the argument parser was reworked: wrong
defaults, a --record-mode flag whose meaning had moved to --record-type,
and no mention of the YAML config file, sub-streams, or Jetson support.

Split it into task-oriented pages under docs/ so the documentation is
versioned alongside the code it describes:

  ARCHITECTURE.md        module layout and frame flow
  CONFIGURATION.md       full flag reference, YAML config file
  CAMERA_AND_ENCODING.md camera backends, encoding pipelines
  SIGNALING.md           MQTT, WHEP, SFU
  RECORDING.md           on-disk layout, rotation, on-demand capture
  ADVANCED.md            how-to guides carried over from the wiki
  COMMERCIAL.md          commercially licensed features

Commercially licensed options are listed with their open-source
counterparts and marked with a [*] linking to COMMERCIAL.md.

Point the README at docs/ instead of the wiki.

docs: correct the recording pipeline and viewer claims

The hardware-encoding diagrams still showed recording going through OpenH264.
RecorderManager::CreateVideoRecorder has picked a hardware encoder since the
V4L2/Jetson recorders landed: an h264 camera source is copied into the MP4
as-is, anything else is encoded by a second hardware encoder instance, and
OpenH264 is only the fallback when --hw-accel is off or the platform has no
hardware encoder. Fix the mjpeg and i420 diagrams, spell out the rule, and add
the recorder's encoder to the architecture graph.

Also:
- Replace "1,000+ viewers" with the claim that actually holds without a
  benchmark to back it: the device uploads one stream regardless of audience.
- Note that on Trixie the default camera_auto_detect=1 is already enough for a
  USB camera, so the legacy V4L2 section is only needed for CSI.

- Collapse the 14 documentation links to a single line pointing at
  picamera.live/docs, and add the missing Commercial and License sections.
- Fix the badge repo slug and the demo alt text, which said Pi 4b.

Delete three unreferenced assets (34 MB): the README images are served from
user-attachments, so these were only the pre-upload originals.

ci: rebuild picamera.live when docs change

picamera.live renders docs/*.md at build time. Cloudflare watches the
picamera-site repo, so a change here produces no commit it can see and the
published docs go stale. Poke its deploy hook instead.

Needs CF_PAGES_DEPLOY_HOOK on this repository. The job fails loudly when the
secret is missing rather than silently skipping the rebuild.
